metadata.content: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Paris Fury retracts claim her husband has been diagnosed with schizophrenia | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Paris Fury retracts claim her husband has been diagnosed with schizophrenia Paris Fury says Tyson did not receive a diagnosis of schizophrenia; Netflix documentary has now been updated; The British Boxing Board of Control indicated it would look into comments about a schizophrenia diagnosis and could deny Fury a licence to face Anthony Joshua on December 11 Thursday 26 November 2026 23:20, UK Image: Tyson Fury has previously spoken about his struggles with mental health Paris Fury has retracted her claim that husband Tyson Fury was diagnosed with schizophrenia. A new Netflix documentary explores Tyson Fury's experiences of depression, anxiety and bipolar disorder, which became particularly acute after his unified heavyweight championship victory over Wladimir Klitschko in 2015. Paris Fury made the comments about schizophrenia in an initial version of the documentary. Netflix said it has worked to "update" the footage in light of her clarification. She has now said: "I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary. I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson's condition and I used the word 'schizophrenic'. metadata.content: Tonda Eckert: Southampton boss wants to close the chapter on 'Spygate' ahead of Middlesbrough reunion | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Tonda Eckert: Southampton boss wants to close the chapter on 'Spygate' ahead of Middlesbrough reunion Tonda Eckert speaks to Sky Sports News reporter Mark McAdam about 'Spygate' fallout, their points deduction and reunion with Middlesbrough. Watch Southampton vs Middlesbrough live on Sky Sports Football from 7.30pm on Friday night; kick-off 8pm. Mark McAdam Sky Sports News Reporter Thursday 26 November 2026 19:28, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player During this access all areas at Southampton, Saints boss Tonda Eckert opens up on the club moving on from 'Spygate' and their promotion aspirations for this season "I think we've experienced a little bit more in the last 12 months than normal." It may be the understatement of the century, but it's not a huge surprise considering Tonda Eckert is a relatively understated man. The storm of 'Spygate' is over, but the aftershock is still being felt. Southampton are sixth in the table, seven points behind leaders Middlesbrough ahead of their reunion on Friday night - live on Sky Sports . Were it not for the four-point deduction, the gap would be smaller. Were it not for the entire controversy, the Saints would possibly be in the Premier League right now.
